correctness.rationale: The original circle angular derivative is minimized at u=1 and gives precisely y<(1-x)/(3+x); Radó–Kneser–Choquet gives disk diffeomorphism. Exact Laurent coefficients c1,c2,c_-1 and their geometric tails yield closed forms for the disk-normalized harmonic map and Hadamard square. An exact two-point divided-difference identity bounds analytic and coanalytic differences separately. The positive rational factorization of Lambda proves a global co-Lipschitz inequality and, via derivative limits, strictly positive Jacobian everywhere. A SymPy checker was run successfully against the complete bundled code; finite parameter sanity checks are auxiliary, not infinite proofs.

originality.rationale: A two-real-parameter global disk-normalized Hadamard self-square preservation theorem with positive co-Lipschitz constant is not implied by the inspected main paper (which real-affine-normalizes to an ellipse and proves the opposite local phenomenon), or by four full published notes about that ellipse map. Indexed searches for disk-target normalization, co-Lipschitz self-square, dual aliases and potential broader harmonic convolution classes did not find the stated implication. Older specialized half-plane/strip papers were checked at abstract level and remain an explicit residual risk.
residual_risks: An unindexed general disk-target harmonic convolution preservation theorem could subsume the statement.
Broad early harmonic convolution references were not all inspected in full; the closest source and four closest public records were.
The co-Lipschitz constant need not be best possible for y>0; theorem asserts only a valid positive lower bound.

value.rationale: The 2026 bounded convex harmonic counterexample makes the choice of normalization a substantive mathematical issue: its original Poisson disk-target map and its ellipse-normalized counterpart have different convolution coefficients. The new complete two-real-parameter preservation theorem and uniform positive lower bound identify a natural positive region, rather than an arbitrary parameter slice, and provide stable inversion estimates for the disk-target family. It is neither a routine restatement of the ellipse fold calculations nor only a finite experiment. Exactness at the analytic y=0 endpoint and continued strictness arbitrarily close to the circle-diffeomorphism degeneration boundary give natural reference points.
